text:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT 4067890123 — Elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects in us-west-2 (streaming gateway)

incident-bot: Severity: P2. Trigger: alerting rule streaming.gateway.5xx_rate > 3% (5m)
incident-bot: Started: 2026-03-15T03:12:10Z. Current 5m 5xx rate: ~6%. Affected routes: /v1/generate/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Link: https://ops.redwood/incident/4067890123

sara.ops: I'm oncall and jumping in. paging @priya and @jordan. taking lead. :hand:

priya: on it, joining. grabbing logs from ingress and gateway.

jordan: I'm ready to help with routing rollback / config. quick question — is this a client cancel spike or gateway-side error?

kai: I'm pulling traces. I see increased connection resets and partial chunked frames around 03:11:xx. sample log: 
```
[stream-gw] 2026-03-15T03:12:34Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 stream_write failed: write tcp 10.0.5.23:443->10.1.2.4:52341: connection reset by peer
[stream-gw] 2026-03-15T03:12:35Z WARN  request_id=efgh5678 chunk_truncated len=0 expected=512
```

miguel.support: Support is seeing customer reports from AcmeAnalytics (large streaming sessions) — partial transcripts + reconnect loops. Noticed ~20 tickets opened in last 10m.

sara.ops: Initial mitigation plan (15m window):
- flip route-level fallback to paged responses for streaming endpoints in us-west-2
- reduce gateway concurrency per-client to 50
- enable aggressive keepalive probes on gateway to detect dead clients faster
- temporarily disable prefix-KV caching for streaming to see if cache corruption is involved

jordan: Commands I'm about to run (will comment when done):
```
# failover streaming -> paged for us-west-2
rtr route update --region=us-west-2 --route=/v1/generate/stream --set=fallback=paged --ttl=15m

# throttle per-client
rtr gateway set-throttle --region=us-west-2 --max-rps=50

# restart ingress gateway to clear stuck connections
kubectl -n streaming rollout restart deploy/ingress-gateway-usw2
```

priya: I'll toggle failover and watch SLOs. Jordan, please hold on cache toggle until I attach traces.

eng-runtime: Noted. If restart hurts capacity we can temporarily spin up a small extra pool: `dedicated-pool-usw2-hotfix` (2x g4dn). Want confirmation before scaling.

sara.ops: Go ahead and provision 2 nodes as precaution. miguel, tell support to set expectation to "degraded streaming — paged fallback enabled" to impacted customers.

miguel.support: Noted. Messaging template: "We're seeing elevated errors on streaming responses in us-west-2; we've enabled a temporary non-streaming fallback while we investigate. No data loss reported; sessions might require reconnect. We're monitoring and will update every 15m."

kai: Traces show frequent FIN from upstream clients ~50ms after first chunk, then gateway attempts to write and gets EPIPE. Hypothesis: certain clients drop long-lived streaming connections when internal buffers exceed ~256KB. Could be regression in chunked flush behaviour after last runtime change to the write buffer.

sara.ops: Good hypothesis. Priya, can you roll back the runtime commit that tweaked streaming flush behaviour if we confirm?

priya: I can. Identified PR: `runtime/streaming: reduce-buffer-flush` merged 2026-03-14 22:40 UTC. I'll stage a rollback to to-be-confirmed candidate. But first keep paged fallback on and watch for 5xx drop.

jordan: Failover executed. `rtr` returned success. Gateway throttle applied. `kubectl` restart triggered — pods are terminating and new pods are coming up.

incident-bot: Action log recorded: failover -> paged (us-west-2), throttle -> 50rps, ingress restart.

sara.ops: Metrics update?

kai: 03:22:00Z snapshot after mitigations: 5xx rate dropped to 1.4% (5m). Connection resets down ~60%. Streaming traffic decreased as expected due to fallback.

miguel.support: Ticket surge reduced, AcmeAnalytics reporting degraded but usable.

nora: Product wants a short post for customers: a one-paragraph summary + ETA for full restoration. I can draft if you give root cause.

priya: Still investigating root cause. Tentative: a buffer flush regression in runtime that interacts poorly with certain client read-scheduling; rollback candidate ready if needed.

sara.ops: Current plan: keep paged fallback for 30m, monitor error rate and reconnect patterns. If 5xx <= 0.5% and customers stable, we'll keep paged for the rest of the day while eng-runtime validates rollback locally. If spike returns, escalate to oncall-P1.

jordan: I've pushed a temporary feature-flag to disable the new flush behavior on canary nodes: `ff/runtime.disable_flush_regression=true` for us-west-2. Patch: 
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/runtime-canary FF_DISABLE_FLUSH_REGRESSION=true
```

priya: Canary picked up flag; canary logs show chunk writes go through without truncation. rolling more nodes now.

kai: Observability note — enable `streaming.chunk.trace=1` for a short window to capture any future truncations.

sara.ops: Handoff: Jordan will take next 4h watch starting 04:00 UTC. Handoff notes: paged fallback active, throttle=50rps, runtime flag applied to canaries, ingress restarted, provisioned 2 extra nodes (monitor cost). Watch metrics: https://ops.redwood/metrics/streaming/us-west-2 (SLO pane). If 5xx > 3% for 10m, escalate page to eng-runtime and on-call SRE lead.

jordan: Acknowledged. I'll keep the paged fallback and observe. Will also coordinate with eng-runtime for the rollback if canary looks good.

sara.ops: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident page and set next update 04:00 UTC. Closing live mitigation phase.

incident-bot: Incident 4067890123 updated: status = "mitigated (live)"; next update 2026-03-15T04:00:00Z. Link: https://ops.redwood/incident/4067890123/notes

sara.ops: Final note for handoff: collect client IDs showing repeated FINs and attach to incident doc for customer outreach. (I'll export list and put in the ticket.)

miguel.support: Support will prepare customer follow-ups and include list from sara when provided.

jordan: Oncall takeover in 5m. will maintain. :thumbsup:
